'''Nikola Mirotić Stajović''' ([[Serbian Cyrillic alphabet|Serbian Cyrillic]]: Никола Митровић Стајовић); born 11 February 1991) is a Montenegrin–born naturalized Spanish professional basketball player for [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. The [[power forward]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACB.com Spanish ACB League official player profile |url=http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=BGK |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605214322/http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=BGK |archive-date=5 June 2013 |access-date=19 April 2011 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.playerID_58753.compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.season_2010.roundID_7339.teamID_362.html |title=NIKOLA MIROTIC (SPAIN) |publisher=Fibaeurope.com |access-date=9 July 2012}}</ref> is a five-time [[All-EuroLeague Team]] member, and previously played for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Liga ACB. Mirotić was drafted with the 23rd pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]], and played in the [[NBA]] from 2014 for the [[Chicago Bulls]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and [[Milwaukee Bucks]], before returning to Spain in the 2019 offseason.

==Early life==
Growing up in [[Montenegro]], [[Association football|football]] was Mirotić's true passion. As he got older, his family realized his height could be a lot more useful for another sport. At the age of 13, his grandfather introduced him to basketball.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/analysis/235170/How-Nikola-Mirotic-Rose-From-Soccer-Destiny-To-European-Phenom-To-The-NBA How Nikola Mirotic Rose From Soccer Destiny, To European Phenom, To The NBA]</ref> Mirotić started playing basketball with the Joker School in [[Podgorica]]<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=77449 Las lecciones aprendidas de Nikola Mirotic y Marko Todorovic] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180419183510/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=77449 |date=19 April 2018 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref> run by retired professional basketball player [[Jadran Vujačić]].

In the summer of 2005, at the age of 14, Mirotić signed a junior contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].

== Professional career ==

===Real Madrid (2008–2014)===
After playing for the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid juniors]] from 2006 to 2008, Mirotić signed with the Real Madrid senior team in 2008. During the [[2010–11 Euroleague]] season, he emerged as one of his team's most valuable players, and won the [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/84950/180 |title=Real Madrid's Nikola Mirotic chosen 2011 Rising Star |publisher=Euroleague.net |access-date=9 July 2012}}</ref> In April 2011, he signed a five-year contract extension with Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/84995 |title=Real Madrid extends Mirotic through 2016 |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=26 April 2011 |access-date=9 July 2012}}</ref> With Real Madrid, he won the [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|Spanish King's Cup]] and the [[Spanish Supercup (basketball)|Spanish Supercup]] in 2012.
[[File:Mirotic-Madrid-CB Sevilla marzo 2013 cropped.jpg|thumb|150px|Mirotić with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in 2013]]

On 23 June 2011, Mirotić was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 23rd overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He was later traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and again to the [[Chicago Bulls]] on draft night.<ref>{{cite news |title=NBA Draft: Nr 1 dla Irvinga, wybrano 10 Europejczyków |url=http://polskikosz.pl/news/102855/nba_draft__nr_1_dla_irvinga__wybrano_10_europejczy.html |work=PolskiKosz.pl |date=24 June 2011 |access-date=2 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628025204/http://www.polskikosz.pl/news/102855/nba_draft__nr_1_dla_irvinga__wybrano_10_europejczy.html |archive-date=28 June 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the [[2012–13 Euroleague]] season, he finished second in the EuroLeague Rising Star voting to [[Kostas Papanikolaou]],<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/112909/180/rising-star-trophy-winner-kostas-papanikolaou-olympiacos-piraeus Euroleague.net Rising Star Trophy winner: Kostas Papanikolaou, Olympiacos Piraeus.]</ref> and he was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Second Team]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/113030/180 Euroleague.net 2012-13 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced.]</ref> In May 2014, he was named to the All-EuroLeague Second Team, for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web|title=2013-14 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/136869|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=9 May 2014}}</ref>

In a total of 97 EuroLeague games for Real Madrid, Mirotić averaged 10.8 points and 4.5 rebounds per game.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=000796#!careerstats MIROTIC, NIKOLA – Euroleague.net]</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2014–2018)===
====2014–15 season====
On 18 July 2014, Mirotić signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Bulls sign forward Nikola Mirotic|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-forward-nikola-mirotic|access-date=18 July 2014|work=NBA.com|date=18 July 2014}}</ref> to a reported three-year, $16.6 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls Sign Nikola Mirotic To Three-Year, $16.6M Deal|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234358/Bulls-Sign-Nikola-Mirotic-To-Three-Year-$166M-Deal|work=RealGM.com|date=18 July 2014|access-date=18 July 2014}}</ref> In addition, Mirotić was required to pay $3 million to Real Madrid for his contract buyout.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nikola Mirotic is the best paid European rookie in NBA history|url=http://hoopshype.com/articles/hoopshype/nikola-mirotic-is-the-best-paid-euro-rookie-in-nba-history|work=HoopsHype.com|date=22 July 2014|access-date=22 July 2014|archive-date=24 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140724145450/http://hoopshype.com/articles/hoopshype/nikola-mirotic-is-the-best-paid-euro-rookie-in-nba-history|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 19 December 2014, Mirotić scored a then career-high 27 points, as he converted all six of his three-pointers, in a 103–97 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Butler, Mirotic lead Bulls over Grizzlies 103-97|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141219/CHIMEM/gameinfo.html|access-date=20 December 2014|work=NBA.com|date=19 December 2014}}</ref> On 5 January 2015, he was named the Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in December.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/nikola-mirotic-named-kia-nba-eastern-conference-rookie-month NIKOLA MIROTIC NAMED KIA NBA EASTERN CONFERENCE ROOKIE OF THE MONTH]</ref> During the NBA's All-Star Weekend, Mirotić played for World Team in the Rising Stars Challenge. He scored 16 points on 6-of-9 shooting from the field in the World's 121–112 win over Team USA.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/bulls/post/_/id/21542 Mirotic shines among young stars]</ref> On 1 March, he scored a career-high 29 points in a loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150301/LACCHI/gameinfo.html |title=Chris Paul, DeAndre Jordan lead Clippers past Bulls 96-86 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=3 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405024454/http://www.nba.com/games/20150301/LACCHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=5 April 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> With injuries impacting teammates during the month of March, Mirotić was expected to fill a larger role for his team. He averaged 20.8 points and 7.6 rebounds while playing 30.8 minutes per game.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mirotni01/gamelog/2015/ Nikola Mirotic 2014-15 Game Log]</ref><ref>[http://www.nba.com/2015/news/features/steve_aschburner/03/19/chicago-bulls-nikola-mirotic-paying-off-in-march-for-team/ Bulls in thick of East chase thanks to Mirotic's big month]</ref> In his rookie season, Mirotić averaged 10.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 82 games,<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mirotni01.html Nikola Mirotic NBA Stats]</ref> giving him the recognition as a candidate for the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year Award]].<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2015/04/29/andrew-wiggins-reportedly-set-to-be-named-nba-rookie-of-the-year/ Andrew Wiggins reportedly set to be named NBA rookie of the year]</ref> Mirotić finished second in Rookie of the Year voting with 335 votes behind [[Andrew Wiggins]] who received 604 votes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/30/kia-nba-rookie-of-the-year-2014-15-official-release/index.html|title=Timberwolves' Andrew Wiggins wins 2014-15 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year Award|date=30 April 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=30 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150504000335/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/30/kia-nba-rookie-of-the-year-2014-15-official-release/index.html|archive-date=4 May 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He played his first post-season game in the NBA on 18 April 2015 in game 1 of the Bulls' first-round series match-up against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. In 13 minutes off the bench, he recorded 5 points and 5 rebounds.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150418/MILCHI/gameinfo.html Rose scores 23, Bulls beat Bucks 103-91]</ref>

====2015–16 season====
At the beginning of the 2015–16 season, Mirotić had a starting role ahead of All-Star center [[Joakim Noah]]. He scored a team-high 19 points in the season opening win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/CLECHI/gameinfo.html |title=With Obama watching, Bulls hold off Cavaliers 97-95 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=31 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151028011548/http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/CLECHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=28 October 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He started in all 18 games to begin the season, coming off the bench for the first time on 9 December against the [[Boston Celtics]], scoring 10 points in 22 minutes of action.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151209/CHIBOS/gameinfo.html |title=Thomas carries Boston to 105-100 win over Chicago |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=10 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151209202505/http://www.nba.com/games/20151209/CHIBOS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=9 December 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He continued coming off the bench following 9 December, in a back-up role to [[Taj Gibson]].<ref>[http://www.realtytoday.com/articles/61123/20151211/nba-rumors-major-change-chicago-bulls-roster-taj-gibson-nikola.htm NBA Rumors: A Major Change in Chicago Bulls Roster, Taj Gibson and Nikola Mirotic Affected]</ref> His next start came on 21 December against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], as he started at small forward in place of [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20151221/BKNCHI/gameinfo.html Lopez, Young lead Nets to 105-102 victory over Bulls]</ref> On 1 January, he recorded 17 points and a career-high seven assists in a 108–81 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160101/NYKCHI/gameinfo.html Butler helps Bulls pull away from Knicks for 108-81 victory]</ref> On 27 January, he was diagnosed with an acute appendicitis and was subsequently ruled out until after the All-Star break.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/nikola-mirotic-injury-update NIKOLA MIROTIC INJURY UPDATE]</ref> He returned to action on 5 March against the [[Houston Rockets]] after missing 16 games.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mirotni01/gamelog/2016/ Nikola Mirotic 2015-16 Game Log]</ref> On 23 March, he scored a career-high 35 points in a loss to the New York Knicks.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160323/NYKCHI/gameinfo.html |title=Porzingis ties career high with 29, Knicks top Bulls 115-107 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=24 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161103203229/http://www.nba.com/games/20160323/NYKCHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=3 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
On 26 December 2016, less than two weeks after falling out of the rotation for a couple of games, Mirotić recorded a then-season-high 20 points in a 90–85 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899907|title=Mirotic, Wade lead Bulls over Pacers 90-85 to snap skid at 3|work=ESPN.com|date=26 December 2016|access-date=27 December 2016}}</ref> After not playing by coach's decision in two straight games in early March so that management and the coaching staff could look at [[Joffrey Lauvergne]], Mirotić landed on the inactive list.<ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-nikola-mirotic-inactive-status-bits-spt-0313-20170312-story.html|title=Nikola Mirotic's fall from grace reaches new low with inactive status|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=12 March 2017|access-date=13 March 2017}}</ref> On 13 March, he returned from a three-game absence and scored 24 points on five three-pointers in a 115–109 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900386|title=Rondo provides spark as starter, Bulls top Hornets 115-109|work=ESPN.com|date=13 March 2017|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref> On 22 March, he scored a season-high 28 points in a 117–95 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900456|title=Mirotic scores season-high 28, Bulls beat Pistons 117-95|work=ESPN.com|date=22 March 2017|access-date=23 March 2017}}</ref> Four days later, he tied his season high with another 28-point effort in a 109–94 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900485|title=Butler did it: Bulls pull away for 109-94 win over Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=26 March 2017|access-date=26 March 2017}}</ref> He had a third 28-point game on 30 March in a 99–93 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He had six three-pointers against both Milwaukee and Cleveland, becoming the first Bulls player to hit six or more three-pointers in back-to-back games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900517|title=Bulls top Cavs 99-93, James moves to 7th on NBA scoring list|work=ESPN.com|date=30 March 2017|access-date=30 March 2017}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
On 25 September 2017, Mirotić re-signed with the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-re-sign-nikola-mirotic|title=BULLS RE-SIGN NIKOLA MIROTIC|work=NBA.com|date=26 September 2017|access-date=26 September 2017}}</ref> On 17 October 2017, Mirotić was sent to the hospital after engaging in a physical altercation with teammate [[Bobby Portis]] during practice. Portis punched Mirotić in the face resulting in Mirotić suffering a concussion and multiple facial fractures.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21056581|title=Bulls' Nikola Mirotic suffers broken facial bones in altercation with teammate Bobby Portis|work=ESPN.com|date=17 October 2017|access-date=17 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-nikola-mirotic-bobby-portis-fight-bulls-practice-20171017-story.html|title=Bulls' Nikola Mirotic out with two broken bones in face after being punched by teammate Bobby Portis|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=17 October 2017|access-date=17 October 2017}}</ref> Mirotić made his season debut on 8 December, scoring six points in 14 minutes in a 119–111 overtime win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975118|title=Markkanen scores 24, Bulls end skid with OT win over Hornets|work=ESPN.com|date=8 December 2017|access-date=8 December 2017}}</ref> On 11 December, he scored 24 points in his first start of the season in a 108–85 win over the [[Boston Celtics]]. He hit 9 of 14 shots and grabbed eight rebounds in his third appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975142|title=Mirotic, Portis lead way, Bulls blow out Celtics 108-85|work=ESPN.com|date=11 December 2017|access-date=11 December 2017}}</ref> On 13 December, he scored 29 points on 11-of-18 shooting with nine rebounds in a 103–100 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975160|title=Bulls beat Jazz 103-100 for 4th straight victory|work=ESPN.com|date=13 December 2017|access-date=14 December 2017}}</ref> On 26 December, he came off the bench to score 24 points in 28 minutes, as the Bulls won for the eighth time in 10 games, beating the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] 115–106.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975247|title=Mirotic scores 24 points off bench, Bulls beat Bucks 115-106|work=ESPN.com|date=26 December 2017|access-date=26 December 2017}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2018–2019)===

2018 first-round pick and the right to swap 2021 second-round picks with the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans Acquire Nikola Mirotić|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-nikola-mirotic|access-date=1 February 2018|work=NBA.com|date=1 February 2018}}</ref> He made his debut for the Pelicans two days later, scoring 18 points in a 118–107 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975526|title=Butler scores 30 to lead Wolves past Pelicans, 118-107|work=ESPN.com|date=3 February 2018|access-date=4 February 2018}}</ref> On 10 February, he recorded 21 points and 16 rebounds in a 138–128 double-overtime win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975572|title=Davis has 44, Pelicans blow 28-point lead, top Nets in 2 OTs|work=ESPN.com|date=10 February 2018|access-date=10 ===Barcelona (2019–2023)===

====2019–20 season====
On 6 July 2019, Mirotić signed a three-year deal, with the option of an extension through to 2023, with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Nikola Mirotic signs for Barça |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/1265482/nikola-mirotic-signs-for-barca |access-date=6 July 2019 |work=www.fcbarcelona.com |date=6 July 2019}}</ref> According to sources, Mirotić's contract was worth [[€]]26 million, making him the highest-paid basketball player in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/904004/mirotics-salary-reportedly-between-e-39m-and-e-52-per-season/|title=Mirotic's salary reportedly between € 3,9Μ and € 5,2 per season|date=7 July 2019|work=Eurohoops|access-date=7 July 2019}}</ref> On 27 June 2020, Mirotic was awarded the league's Most Valuable Player award. He became the fifth player in [[Liga Endesa]] history to have multiple MVP awards, joining [[Darryl Middleton]], [[Arvydas Sabonis]], [[Luis Scola]] and [[Felipe Reyes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acb.com/articulo/ver/153512-nikola-mirotic-es-el-mvp-movistar-de-la-liga-endesa.html|title=Nikola Mirotic es el MVP Movistar de la Liga Endesa|publisher=ACB.com|date=27 June 2020|access-date=27 June 2020}}</ref> Mirotić finished the season averaging 19.5 points and 5.7 rebounds per game. He extended his contract until 2025 on 25 September 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Barcelona, Nikola Mirotic agree on contract extension |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/barcelona-nikola-mirotic-agree-on-contract-extension/ |website=Sportando |access-date=25 September 2020 |date=25 September 2020 |last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref>

====2021–22 season====
In the 2021–22 season, he won his first [[EuroLeague MVP]] award, becoming the first Barcelona player to win the award in 14 years.<ref>{{cite news |title=2021-22 Turkish Airlines EuroLeague MVP: Nikola Mirotic, FC Barcelona {{!}} Euroleague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/2021-22-turkish-airlines-euroleague-mvp-nikola-mirotic-fc-barcelona/ |access-date=20 May 2022 |work=Euroleague Basketball}}</ref>

====2022–23 season====
On 22 July 2022, Mirotić suffered an Achilles injury that ruled him out for the beginning of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-175554-nikola-mirotic-reportedly-suffers-achilles-injury.html|title= Nikola Mirotic reportedly suffers Achilles injury|date=July 22, 2022|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 1 December 2022, Mirotić made his season debut against [[Alba Berlin]], finishing the game with 19 points, 6 rebounds, 3 steals, and 2 assists in an 88–86 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-181791-nikola-mirotic-reacts-to-his-return-on-the-court.html|title=Nikola Mirotic reacts to his return on the court|date=December 2, 2022|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 15 May 2023, Mirotić was named into the All-EuroLeague Second Team alongside [[Mike James (basketball, born 1990)|Mike James]] from [[AS Monaco Basket]], [[Kevin Punter]] from [[KK Partizan]], [[Darius Thompson]] from [[Saski Baskonia]], and [[Wade Baldwin IV]] from [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-189530-all-euroleague-second-team-revealed.html|title=All-EuroLeague Second Team revealed|date=May 15, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 19 May 2023, Mirotić and [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet]] failed to win the EuroLeague despite reaching the third Final Four in a row. Barcelona lost in the semifinal against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] 66–78.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-189715-edy-tavares-monster-game-leads-real-madrid-to-triumph-over-barca-final-vs-olympiacos.html|title=Edy Tavares' monster game leads Real Madrid to triumph over Barca, final vs. Olympiacos|date=May 19, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

Mirotić finished the game with 3 points (1/10 FG, 1/2 FT), 6 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 steal, and 3 turnovers. He took the responsibility after the game. "I congratulate Real Madrid, they played a great game," Mirotic said. "I take a large part of the responsibility for us losing this game. I haven't been at the level expected of me, I haven't been able to help the team. I feel very bad. I say to our fans that I'm sorry, thank you for supporting us and for coming here."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-189720-mirotic-takes-responsibility-and-apologizes-for-barcas-loss-i-feel-very-bad.html|title=Mirotic takes responsibility and apologizes for Barca's loss: 'I feel very bad'|date=May 20, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 20 July 2023, [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet]] officially announced that the club is unilaterally terminating Mirotić's contract. Mirotić still had two years left in his contract, but he became a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-192089-nikola-mirotic-and-barcelona-part-ways-the-case-will-go-to-court.html|title=Nikola Mirotic and Barcelona part ways, the case will go to court|date=July 20, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

===2023 free agency===
On 28 June 2023, [[Olimpia Milano]] head coach [[Ettore Messina]] said that Milan can't compete with the likes of Anadolu Efes, Fenerbahçe, Panathinaikos, Barcelona, or Real Madrid in the race to sign Mirotić, essentially denying a previous report about a deal between the two sides.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-191256-ettore-messina-on-signing-mirotic-we-cant-compete-with-other-clubs.html|title=Ettore Messina on signing Mirotic: 'We can't compete with other clubs'|date=June 28, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 9 July 2023, reports in the Greek media emerged stating that [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] entered the race for Mirotić's signature, offering a two-year €8 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-191805-panathinaikos-join-the-race-for-nikola-mirotics-signature.html|title=Panathinaikos join the race for Nikola Mirotic's signature|date=July 9, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

However, on 23 July 2023, Panathinaikos owner [[Dimitrios Giannakopoulos]] denied the rumors about the interest in Mirotić. "I looked at my iPad, and there are 10,000 messages," Giannakopoulos said on Saturday via his Instagram. "Now, even our plane is being watched, it is said that we went to Serbia to make a deal with [Nikola] Mirotić. No, we were at The Weeknd concert."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-192444-dimitris-giannakopoulos-addresses-nikola-mirotics-rumors.html|title=Dimitris Giannakopoulos addresses Nikola Mirotic's rumors|date=July 23, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 16 July 2023, the Serbian media reported that Mirotić landed in Belgrade to finalize an agreement with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]]. Partizan head coach [[Željko Obradović]] reportedly had the biggest influence on Mirotić's decision to join the Serbian powerhouse.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-192090-nikola-mirotic-on-the-verge-of-joining-partizan.html|title=Nikola Mirotic on the verge of joining Partizan|date=July 16, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 22 July 2023, two days after officially parting ways with Barcelona, Mirotić stated that he wouldn't join Partizan due to insults and threats he received after news of his continuation in Obradović's team was published.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-192419-nikola-mirotic-will-not-continue-his-career-in-serbia.html|title=Nikola Mirotic will not continue his career in Serbia|date=July 22, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref> Hours after the player's statement, Partizan responded by releasing a statement of their own, claiming that Mirotić's decision had nothing to do with the supposed threats. "The club publicly calls on Nikola Mirotić, out of his commitment to the truth, and he is a man who fights for the truth, to say who the people who threatened him are. The club's wish and plan was to build the team around the players who are currently under contract and Mirotić himself, but now that plan will have to be corrected. KK Partizan Mozzart Bet firmly believes that the reasons for not signing the contract by Nikola Mirotić have nothing to do with any threats but with some other things that the public will be able to see for themselves in the days ahead," Partizan wrote in the statement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-192420-partizan-call-out-nikola-mirotic-for-his-statement.html|title=Partizan call out Nikola Mirotic for his statement|date=July 22, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

On 5 October 2023, Partizan head coach Željko Obradović claimed Mirotić received pressure from unnamed politicians and church members after his decision to join the Serbian powerhouse.

"I will tell you exactly as he told me. He didn't mention any names, but he told me he received calls from politicians and the church. Nikola did not reveal any names, but he told me it was about people from politics and the church. I know that much. He can confirm that," Obradović said in an interview with news magazine Nedeljnik.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-195401-zeljko-obradovic-claims-mirotic-was-pressured-not-to-join-partizan.html|title=Zeljko Obradovic claims Mirotic was pressured not to join Partizan|date=October 5, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

However, on 2 November 2023, Mirotić denied the claims and rumors about being influenced by the Serbian Orthodox Church not to join Partizan.

"Wanting to debunk the slander that seeks to harm our Holy Church and its Patriarch, I have the need to state that I have not yet had the honor to meet His Holiness [[Porfirije, Serbian Patriarch|Patriarch Porfirije]] nor to communicate with him, directly or indirectly," Mirotić wrote in a post on Instagram.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-196800-nikola-mirotic-responds-to-rumors-church-caused-his-partizan-denial.html|title=Nikola Mirotic responds to rumors church caused his Partizan denial|date=November 2, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

==National team career==
Mirotić was a member of the junior national team of Spain. He helped [[Spain men's national under-20 basketball team|Spain's U20 national team]] win the bronze medal at the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2010]] [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he was named to the All-Tournament Team. He also led Spain to the gold medal in [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2011]]. Mirotić was the top scorer and [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship#Awards|MVP]] of the tournament, averaging 27 points (tournament record) and 10 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news |title=MVP Mirotic leads All Tournament Team |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_e6ae3P12HGcnr-ChPqaeU0.articleMode_on.html |work=fibaeurope.com |date=24 July 2011 |access-date=25 July 2011}}</ref>

In June 2015, Mirotić was named by [[head coach]] [[Sergio Scariolo]] as one of 17 candidates to try out for the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team]] that would play at the [[EuroBasket 2015]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gasol, Mirotic on powerful Spain roster|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_vWsMX9dJHOkwZ2304LPIA3.articleMode_on.html|access-date=8 August 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=30 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150826083317/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_vWsMX9dJHOkwZ2304LPIA3.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=26 August 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> Mirotić made Spain's final 12-man roster, and he went on to win a gold medal at the tournament, in September 2015. He also played with Spain at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]], where he won a bronze medal.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120928065837/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/q/Nikola%20Mirotic/pid/_/players.html Nikola MIROTIC (ESP).]</ref>

On January 19, 2023, Mirotić confirmed he's retiring from the Spanish national team. "I haven't played with them for many years, I've focused a lot on giving my all to the club I'm at. Then in summer, I have many personal things, family, my businesses. And I am at an age, especially after having the injury and everything, in which I don't see myself returning with the national team," Mirotić explained.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-184037-nikola-mirotic-announces-his-retirement-from-the-spanish-national-team.html|title=Nikola Mirotic announces his retirement from the Spanish national team|date=January 19, 2023|website=BasketNews}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mirotić and his wife, Nina Vujačić, have one son. His wife is the daughter of his former coach and mentor, Jadran Vujačić, who also played professional basketball with [[KK Borac Čačak|Borac Čačak]], [[KK Partizan]] and [[Budućnost Titograd]].<ref>[http://grantland.com/features/nikola-mirotic-chicago-bulls-toni-kukoc-pau-gasol/ Internationally Known, Locally Respected]</ref>

Mirotić is an ethnic [[Serbs of Montenegro|Serb]] and a [[Serbian Orthodox Church|Serbian Orthodox Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-07 |title=Mirotić: Ja sam Crnogorac, srpski pravoslavac |url=https://meridiansport.me/kosarka/mirotic-ja-sam-crnogorac-srpski-pravoslavac/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |language=bs-BA}}</ref> He received the [[Order of St. Sava]] in May 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nikomirotic.com/#makes_me_proud|title=Nikola Mirotic - Official Website|last=Gentlemen|first=Designer &|website=www.nikomirotic.com|language=en|access-date=22 October 2018|archive-date=15 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115200725/https://www.nikomirotic.com/#makes_me_proud|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Košarkaš ponosan na Orden Svetog Save |url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/planeta.300.html:667800-Kosarkas-ponosan-na-Orden-Svetog-Save |website=novosti.rs |access-date=30 November 2018}}</ref> Mirotić has participated in [[Lity in Eastern Christianity|prayer walks]] and [[2019–2020 clerical protests in Montenegro|protests]] in [[Podgorica]] against the controversial religious law concerning the [[Serbian Orthodox Church]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jedan od najboljih košarkaša Evrope na čelu kolone: Nikola Mirotić u litiji ka Podgorici (FOTO)|url=https://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:847818-Jedan-od-najboljih-kosarkasa-Evrope-na-celu-kolone-Nikola-Mirotic-u-litiji-ka-Podgorici-FOTO|access-date=26 February 2020|work=[[Večernje novosti]]|date=16 February 2020|language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Mirotić u litiji ka Podgorici (FOTO)|url=https://www.portalanalitika.me/clanak/358986--mirotic-u-litiji-ka-podgorici-foto|access-date=26 February 2020|work=portalanalitika.me|date=16 February 2020|language=cnr}}</ref>
